wedges.title: Build-State Evidence enters through rebuild triage and CI drift review
wedges.trigger_moment: A team needs to explain why a rebuild happened, why CI slowed down, or why a warm build regressed.
wedges.initial_surface: Local or CI-produced build-state pack plus report/diff/doctor receipts.
import_surfaces: Cargo build-analysis / cargo report surfaces when available
proving_grounds: build-dir-layout migration case with explicit caveats
success_signals: Teams attach receipts to build triage instead of relying on anecdotes
At least one migration or perf discussion is resolved faster because the diff is reviewable
anti_goals: Do not begin as a universal build daemon
Do not sell target-dir archaeology as stable truth
wedges.credible_home: companion-first cargo-* tool over bounded Cargo facts
wedges.next_if_proven: Widen to richer cross-run history, more adapters, and deeper doctor flows without pretending Cargo core already solved the review layer.
notes: This is the clearest first wedge because the pain is broad and the imports are already partially real.

wedges.title: Package Intake enters through publish and dependency-admission review
wedges.trigger_moment: A maintainer is about to publish or adopt a dependency and wants explicit route risk, service truth, and waiver posture.
wedges.initial_surface: review/admit/quarantine/waive/recheck kit over local package facts plus crates.io imports
success_signals: Maintainers begin recording explicit review posture before publishing
Dependency-admission decisions include visible waivers and route truth instead of hand-waving
anti_goals: Do not become a universal crate score
Do not erase context behind a binary allow/deny verdict
wedges.credible_home: companion tool or service-adjacent review kit over crates.io truth
wedges.next_if_proven: Widen to richer route families, incident drills, and repeatable review packets without claiming universal package trust.
notes: The service truth is getting stronger, which makes the review wedge clearer rather than less necessary.

wedges.title: Debug Acceptance enters through issue-ready tuple and session exports
wedges.target_user: debugger maintainer or engineer filing a reproducible debug complaint
wedges.trigger_moment: A debugging problem needs to be reproduced, compared across tuples, or handed off with explicit unsupported-state posture.
wedges.initial_surface: tuple cards plus debug session export packs
proving_grounds: one LLDB or GDB tuple family
success_signals: Issues become easier to route because tuple identity travels with them
Session exports reveal unsupported states instead of hiding them
anti_goals: Do not begin as a debugger fork
Do not rely on IDE-only magic with no export format
wedges.credible_home: commons corpus plus companion export tooling
wedges.next_if_proven: Widen to larger tuple families, richer visualizer records, and reusable regression replay corpora.
notes: The first proof is better issue quality and tuple honesty, not a finished debugger UX story.

wedges.title: Safety Readiness enters through gap-assessment and ownership cards
wedges.target_user: team evaluating Rust for a regulated or qualification-sensitive system
wedges.trigger_moment: An organization needs to understand readiness gaps, evidence burdens, and renewal ownership before saying yes to Rust in a sensitive domain.
wedges.initial_surface: freshness-bearing readiness cards and gap receipts
import_surfaces: package and interop evidence where relevant
success_signals: Adoption or procurement conversations become more precise about missing evidence and owner burden
Organizations use the cards to structure internal readiness discussion
anti_goals: Do not collapse many domain-specific obligations into one fake safety badge
wedges.next_if_proven: Widen to more domain packs, interop guidance, and qualification-friendly renewal practice.
notes: This wedge is stewardship-heavy by design; it becomes real when organizations can use it to frame burden honestly.

wedges.title: Compatibility Claims enter through pre-release claim packs
wedges.trigger_moment: A team is about to cut a release and needs a reviewable answer to what changed at the boundary and what remains unknown or waived.
wedges.initial_surface: release-boundary claim pack with diff, witness, and waiver posture
proving_grounds: one rustdoc-JSON-backed claim with format caveat
success_signals: Release decisions carry more explicit claim posture
Reviewers can distinguish supported claims from lossy imports and waivers
anti_goals: Do not claim one universal public-API truth surface
Do not erase lossiness in machine-readable imports
wedges.next_if_proven: Widen to richer witness families and stronger renewal around compatibility posture.
notes: This wedge compounds best after stronger build and package evidence layers are already honest.

wedges.title: Adoption Navigation enters through one conservative domain default
wedges.target_user: newcomer or internal guide choosing a sane starting stack
wedges.trigger_moment: A team needs a conservative starting point for a specific project shape and wants an evidence-bearing default rather than a hype list.
wedges.initial_surface: one conservative domain default with renewal receipts
import_surfaces: existing evidence and claims from stronger seams
proving_grounds: one explicit stale or unsupported path
success_signals: People reuse the default because it is conservative and current
The default survives at least one renewal without silent drift
anti_goals: Do not become a giant portal
Do not pretend breadth before renewal is solved
wedges.next_if_proven: Widen to a small family of defaults only when renewal ownership is explicit.
notes: This wedge is intentionally constrained because renewal burden remains the blocker.

wedges.title: Tooling Contract enters through a thin import kit
wedges.target_user: tool author or assistant workflow maintainer
wedges.trigger_moment: A tool needs machine-usable Rust context and has to choose which imports are safe, fresh enough, and caveated correctly.
wedges.initial_surface: thin import kit over Cargo metadata, rustdoc JSON, and related machine surfaces with explicit provenance
import_surfaces: other bounded machine-readable surfaces such as libtest JSON when available
success_signals: Other wedges stop scraping unstable internals
Consumers can tell what surface a result came from and what caveats still apply
anti_goals: Do not become a magical universal workspace index
Do not claim authority beyond the imported surfaces
wedges.next_if_proven: Widen to additional importers and stronger contracts that serve other wedges without absorbing them.
notes: This wedge is enabling, not empire-building; its success is judged by what it lets other wedges build honestly.
